title: My Site Personalization accessibility
body:
As noted [here](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-Android/pull/21441#pullrequestreview-2427549531):

> I will note that the toggle elements have no description, so navigating controls with a screen reader is near impossible. I suggest we add descriptions that provide context when moving selection to each element—e.g., "Draft posts, your recent draft posts, on switch, double-tap to toggle." We might either add a description to the toggle or grouping the entire row into a single accessible group.
author: CONTRIBUTOR

title: My Site more menu accessibility
body:
As mentioned [here](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-Android/pull/21383#pullrequestreview-2413182465):

> One consideration for a tangential UI button: the menu button (three vertical dots) on the My Site tab lacks contextual information. I.e., a description of "more" requires one to know they are within the "prompts" card, where a description of "more prompts" or "view more prompts" would mitigate any confusion. There are also several "more" buttons on the screen, further reducing clarity. We might consider updating the button description to reduce the cognitive load for users relying upon screen readers.
author: CONTRIBUTOR

title: Accessibility issues with media pickers
body:
As mentioned [here](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-Android/pull/21287#pullrequestreview-2354911185):

> I note that when a search field is focused, a screen reader is unable to access the network offline message. One can only move focus to the visible illustration, which includes the aforementioned odd alt text. I.e., when the search field is focused, it is not clear at all that a lack of network connection will disrupt the experience. If one dismisses the virtual keyboard, then you can move screen reader focus to the error message and retry button. This experience is present within the GIF library, free stock media, and editor media insert flows.

This is related to the following screens:

- GifMediaDataSource - adding to media library from Tenor
- StockMediaDataSource - adding to media library from free photo library
- MediaLibraryDataSource - adding media to a post from WP media library
author: CONTRIBUTOR

title: Improve self-hosted user list for screenreaders
body:
As mentioned [here](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-Android/pull/21275#discussion_r1790401431), the new self-hosted user list could use some accessibility improvements:

> From my perspective, the screen reader experience for this new list could be improved. E.g., swiping up/down moves between individual user items, but merely announces "list" repeatedly, which provides little context.

> We might improve the experience by having the top level list declare the total number of items ("list, 25 of 35 users"), individual items could announce some high-level information ("dcalhoun, administrator"), etc.

title: Accessibility : Gutenberg Audit
body:
This is a list of concerns we found when auditing TalkBack support in Gutenberg. The audit was done using develop (c9578a0), Google Pixel 4 XL, Android 10.

## Concerns

### Block Content Descriptions
All content descriptions seem to contain an unneeded comma.

[image]

### Block Options
Some options announce the row of the block and others, for example, Settings don't do that. We should consider adding the Block type to these so that the user knows which block they are in. It's not totally necessary though, because if they were to switch to another block then it would be announced, nonetheless, it would be a good improvement.

### Video Block
When a video is added the video can be focused/selected but it doesn't state an action that can be performed. In contrast, selecting an image announces it's actions.

### Select Blocks Process

Improving the select block process would be beneficial as I didn't know I had to double-tap to make a block selected until I did some experiments. Also, there are several blocks that can't be selected especially text- …[cut]

title: Information Architecture modification -> Vision Accessibility audit
body:
We need to Audit all the modifications introduced with IA project to ensure we correctly support Vision Accessibility.

Reporting below some note by @shiki as a starting point:

> - Reader: When the filter control is selected, TalkBack just says the filter name (e.g. “All sites”). It doesn’t say that it’s a button or that it’s a filter. It’s not obvious what happens after tapping, basically. It might be better for TalkBack to say something like “Filter, , Button”.
> - Reader: The Settings button is announced as “Unlabeled, Button”.
> - Reader → Filter List: The Sites and Tags are not marked as headings. A heading attribute is useful if you’re navigating by heading with TalkBack.
> - Reader → Filter List: The currently selected filter is not announced by TalkBack as “selected”.
> - My Site: The “Stats”, “Pages”, “Posts”, and “Media” buttons are spoken as “Unlabeled button”.
> - My Site: The “Stats”, “Pages”, “Posts”, and “Media” labels are unnecessarily accessible. Since the buttons (icons) are accessible, these don’t need to be.

title: Reader: each list item has 7 focusable elements which makes it slow to navigate
body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > TalkBack > "Use service" or use the Volume key shortcut.
1. In the WordPress app, go to Reader.
1. Swipe right to navigate through several posts in the list.

**Result:** each list item has 7 focusable elements which makes it slow to navigate. (28s recording)

> Navigation through the list of posts in the Reader view is pretty slow using TalkBack because each post in the list has seven focusable elements. As a result, if a TalkBack user wants to get from , for example, the first post to the fourth post without directly clicking on the fourth post, they have to move to the next item (swipe right) 21 times. This may not be a big deal for light usage, but would be very unpleasant with heavy usage.

[image]

author: CONTRIBUTOR

title: Settings: learn more element should be combined into a single focusable element
body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > TalkBack > "Use service" or use the Volume key shortcut.
1. In the WordPress app, go to My Sites > Settings > More.
1. Swipe right to find the "Learn More" element.

**Result:** (48s recording)

> This part of the Settings – More screen contains two elements that are focusable for TalkBack: (1) the text field, and (2) the learn more button. TalkBack reads the text of the first element (“You can…”) and finishes with “double tap to activate, double tap and hold to long press.” Double-tapping does nothing, however. Double tapping and holding opens a popup dialog. If the learn more button is focused, double tapping opens the same dialog. This could be improved by combining these two focusable elements into a single focusable element that opens the relevant dialog if activated.

title: Accessibility : Post Settings TalkBack Improvements
body:
For this audit the governing principles are as follows (inspired by a previous audit, #7288)

- All the clickable elements should be marked as so.
- All nonactionable and decorative elements should be non-focusable.
- Relevant content should be grouped together.
- All important elements should be described through content description.

* Post Settings
* First option says "Status Draft in pager". Correct the pager reference.
* Second options reads "Publish Immediately, Imediately". One of the "immediately"s need to be removed.

* Excerpt even when set still says "not set". This issue correlates to the avoid so it should be addressed in one go.

title: Masterbar: Add more context to main menu
body:
### Expected behavior

The main menu links in the app, which is similar to the menu on WordPress.com could use more context beyond My Sites, Reader, etc. See the Calypso masterbar logged-in.jsx and logged-out.jsx for strings to be consistent.

title: Reader: Add more context to action buttons on posts
body:
### Expected behavior

When I navigate the Reader in the Android app with a screen reader, I expect to find more context on buttons.

### Actual behavior

* I found the "Visit" icon button was unlabeled. The word "Visit" lacked context for a screen reader user. I want to know what I'm visiting. This can be combined into one button, labeled with "Visit Post Title Name" "Post Title Name" can be hidden visually.
* The Likes button should be labeled with Like "Post Title Name" Has 77 Likes. Or Like "Post Title Name" No Likes yet. You could also communicate state here. So if a post is in a liked state, it could say: Like "Post Title Name" Pressed Has 77 Likes (or No Likes yet).
* Similarly with the Comments button, it needs a more specific label. Comment on "Post Title Name"
* The More button is labeled, but could use more context. "Follow Site Menu" maybe?

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

* Start Talk Back
* Open WordPress app
* Open Reader.
* Begin navigating a list of post by swiping right to navigate forward, reaching the action button area.

* Tested on Nexus 6P, Version Alpha-60.

title: Mono output & L/R balance for ExoPlayer
body:
# System info

**App version**: 2.1.0-RC3

**App source**: Google Play

# Feature description

**Problem you may be having, or feature you want**:
Not the case for me personally, but a portion of our users will have hearing loss on one side. They might benefit from mono output and changing left-right balance. This is already possible when selecting the 'Sonic' media player in the settings, but ExoPlayer is the default and does not support this. Not tech-savvy users may simply see a disabled setting in the player screen and leave it at that. Since ExoPlayer is the default & recommended media player, supporting these features for ExoPlayer would be great.

**Suggested solution**:
> write a custom audio processor for ExoPlayer that is capable of L/R volume and mono downmix (those settings are currently just supported on Sonic)

title: Using double/triple headset button press to fast forward/rewind
body:
**App version:** 1.6.5 (from F-Droid)

**Android version**: 8.0
**Device model**: Sony Xperia XZ2 Compact

As far as I can tell, there's no way to assign multiple headset button presses for fast forwarding or rewinding. Most music players allow to double press the headset button to skip to next song and triple press to skip to the previous one, so I assume it's a system-level setting that treats multiple presses as "media next/media preview" actions. It would be nice to see AntennaPod use do that too instead of just play/pause with a single tap. As far as I know, the only podcast player right now that supports both fast forward AND rewind is Castbox (proprietary).

title: D-Pad Navigation inconsistent
body:
The nextFocus attributes for the layousts seem to be implemented inconsistently with the new UI. Easiest way to test this, is to setup an Android Emulator, and enable Keyboard input for the the Emulator. Then launch the application. Do not use the Mouse to navigate or interact with the application. Just use the Up/Down/Left/Right and Enter keys to navigate the application. You'll find that you can't get to some items, others you get to that have embedded buttons aren't clickable or you can't get the to the button itself.

This is causing issues on devices like Android HDMI Sticks, Google TV, and OUYA devices that are primarily D-Pad navigation. Having to result to the built in touch pad is not a good user experience.

If I get some time, I'll look at providing a patch to address some of these issues for the D-Pad and the related Media Key Codes as well.
